Duration::isvalid¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

Series Duration::isvalid() const

What It Does¶

Tests elementwise whether a Duration position holds a real value rather than the Duration::kNaT missing-value sentinel — the exact negation of isnat at every position.

Parameters¶

None — this is a zero-argument accessor on self.

Returns¶

Series A boolean Series at self’s shape, one test result per position.

Examples¶

Example 1. A valid duration and an explicitly-missing one.

auto one_hour = pluss::duration::hours(1);
auto missing = pluss::duration::nanos(pluss::Duration::kNaT);
std::cout << "valid=" << pluss::series::print(one_hour.isvalid()) << "\n";
std::cout << "missing=" << pluss::series::print(missing.isvalid());

Output¶

valid=Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=true
missing=Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=false

Notes¶

  • isvalid() is always the elementwise negation of isnat() — there is no case where they disagree.

See Also¶

  • isnat: the comparison this negates.

  • fill_nat: replacing missing positions with a real value.

  • where: conditional selection, another mask-driven operation.
